──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n211\t\n212\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n213\t///\n214\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n220\t    Failure,\n221\t    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n222\t    Timeout,\n223\t    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n224\t    AgentNotFound,\n225\t    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n226\t    Interrupted,\n227\t    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n228\t    Crash(i32),\n229\t}\n230\t\n231\timpl Outcome {\n232\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n233\t    ///\n234\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n235\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n236\t    ///\n237\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n238\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n239\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n240\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n241\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n242\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n243\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n244\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n245\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n246\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n247\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n248\t        if was_interrupted {\n249\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n250\t        }\n251\t\n252\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n253\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n254\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n255\t        match exit_code {\n256\t            // Success\n257\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n258\t            // Explicit failure code\n259\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n260\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n261\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n262\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n263\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n264\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n265\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n266\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n267\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n268\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n269\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n270\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n271\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n272\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n273\t        }\n274\t    }\n275\t\n276\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n277\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n278\t        match self {\n279\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n280\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n281\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n282\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n283\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n284\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n285\t        }\n286\t    }\n287\t}\n288\t\n289\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n290\t// DecompositionMode\n291\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n292\t\n293\t/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n294\t///\n295\t/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n296\t/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n297\t///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n298\t///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n299\t///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n300\t/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n301\t///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n302\t///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n303\t///   and consecutive failure count.\n304\t///\n305\t/// # When to use each mode\n306\t///\n307\t/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n308\t/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n309\t/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n310\t/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n311\t/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n312\t///\n313\t/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n314\t/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n315\t/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n316\t/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n317\t/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n318\t///\n319\t/// # API boundary\n320\t///\n321\t/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n322\t/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n323\t/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n324\t#[non_exhaustive]\n325\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n326\t#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\n327\tpub enum DecompositionMode {\n328\t    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n329\t    ///\n330\t    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n331\t    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n332\t    Timeout {\n333\t        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n334\t        timeout_seconds: u64,\n335\t        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n336\t        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n337\t        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n338\t    },\n339\t    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n340\t    ///\n341\t    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n342\t    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n343\t    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n344\t    OrdinaryFailure,\n345\t}\n346\t\n347\timpl DecompositionMode {\n348\t    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n349\t    ///\n350\t    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n351\t    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n352\t    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n353\t    ///\n354\t    /// # },\n495\t}\n496\t\n497\timpl DecompositionDecision {\n498\t    /// Returns true if this decision is to split.\n499\t    pub fn is_split(&self) -> bool {\n500\t        matches!(self, }\n523\t}\n524\t\n525\timpl fmt::Display for DecompositionDecision {\n526\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n527\t        match self {\n528\t DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => {\n532\t                write!(f, \"refuse: {}\", reason)\n533\t            }\n534\t        }\n535\t    }\n536\t}\n537\t\n538\t/// Configuration for decomposition decision thresholds.\n539\t#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n540\tpub struct DecompositionThresholds {\n541\t    /// Minimum timeout (in seconds) required to consider splitting.\n542\t    /// Beads that timed out quickly are likely genuine errors, not size issues.\n543\t    pub min_timeout_seconds: u64,\n544\t    /// Minimum number of retries required to consider splitting.\n545\t    /// Beads should be given multiple chances before decomposition.\n546\t    pub min_retry_count: u32,\n547\t    /// Minimum bead body length (in characters) to consider splitting.\n548\t    /// Beads   DecompositionThresholds {\n558\t            min_timeout_seconds: 300, // 5 minutes\n559\t            min_retry_count: 2,       // Must retry at least twice\n560\t            min_bead_size: 200,       // At least 200 characters\n561\t            child_labels: vec![\n562\t                \"mitosis-child\".to_string(),\n563\t                \"decomposition-child\".to_string(),\n564\t            ],\n565\t        }\n566\t    }\n567\t}\n568\t\n569\t/// Evaluate whether a bead should be decomposed into child beads.\n570\t///\n571\t/// This function implements the decision tree for timeout-driven decomposition.\n572\t/// It evaluates bead characteristics against configured thresholds to determine\n573\t/// whether splitting is appropriate.\n574\t///\n575\t/// # Arguments\n576\t///\n577\t/// * `bead` - The bead to evaluate\n578\t/// * `timeout_seconds` - The timeout duration that was exceeded\n579\t/// * `retry_count` - Number of consecutive retries for this bead\n580\t/// * `thresholds` - Configuration thresholds (uses defaults if None)\n581\t///\n582\t/// # Returns\n583\t///\n584\t/// * `DecompositionDecision::Split` - If criteria are met (proposals must be added by caller)\n585\t/// * `DecompositionDecision::Refuse` - If criteria are not met\n586\t///\n587\t/// # Decision Logic\n588\t///\n589\t/// **Split if ALL of these conditions are met:**\n590\t/// - timeout_seconds >= thresholds.min_timeout_seconds\n591\t/// - retry_count >= thresholds.min_retry_count\n592\t/// - bead body length >= thresholds.min_bead_size\n593\t/// - bead has no assignee (not actively being worked)\n594\t/// - bead has no child labels (not already a decomposed child)\n595\t///\n596\t/// **Refuse if ANY of these conditions are met:**\n597\t/// - Bead body is too small (< min_bead_size)\n598\t/// - Bead has an active assignee\n599\t/// - Bead is already a child (has child labels)\n600\t/// - Timeout is too short (< min_timeout_seconds)\n601\t/// - Not enough retries (< min_retry_count)\n602\t///\n603\t/// # Examples\n604\t///\n605\t/// ```no_run\n606\t/// use needle::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, decompose_bead_decision};\n607\t/// use bead\".to_string(),\n613\t///     body: Some(\"This is a substantial bead body that exceeds 200 characters...\".to_string()),\n614\t///     priority: 2,\n615\t///     status: vec![],\n621\t///     comments: vec![],\n622\t///     created_at: DateTime::from_timestamp(0, 0).unwrap(),\n623\t///     updated_at: DateTime::from_timestamp(0, 0).unwrap(),\n624\t/// };\n625\t///\n626\t/// let decision = decompose_bead_decision(&bead, 600, 3, None);\n627\t/// assert!(decision.is_split());\n628\t/// ```\n629\tpub fn decompose_bead_decision(\n630\t    bead: &Bead,\n631\t    timeout_seconds: u64,\n632\t    retry_count: u32,\n633\t    thresholds: Option<DecompositionThresholds>,\n634\t) -> DecompositionDecision {\n635\t    let thresholds = thresholds.unwrap_or_default();\n636\t\n637\t    // Check if bead is already a child (has child labels)\n638\t    let is_child_bead = bead\n639\t        .labels\n640\t        .iter()\n641\t        .any(|label| thresholds.child_labels.contains(label));\n642\t\n643\t    if is_child_bead {\n644\t        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n645\t            reason: format!(\n646\t                \"bead is already a child bead (has labels: {:?})\",\n647\t                bead.labels\n648\t                    .iter()\n649\t                    .filter(|l| thresholds.child_labels.contains(l))\n650\t                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n651\t            ),\n652\t        };\n653\t    }\n654\t\n655\t    // Check if bead has an active assignee\n656\t    if let Some(assignee) = &bead.assignee {\n657\t        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n658\t            reason: format!(\"bead has active assignee: {}\", assignee),\n659\t        };\n660\t    }\n661\t\n662\t    // Check bead body size\n663\t    let body_size = bead.body.as_ref().map(|b| b.len()).unwrap_or(0);\n664\t    if body_size < thresholds.min_bead_size {\n665\t        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n666\t            reason: format!(\n667\t                \"bead body too small ({} chars < {} minimum)\",\n668\t                body_size, thresholds.min_bead_size\n669\t            ),\n670\t        };\n671\t    }\n672\t\n673\t    // Check timeout threshold\n674\t    if timeout_seconds < thresholds.min_timeout_seconds {\n675\t        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n676\t            reason: format!(\n677\t                \"timeout too short ({}s < {}s minimum)\",\n678\t                timeout_seconds, thresholds.min_timeout_seconds\n679\t            ),\n680\t        };\n681\t    }\n682\t\n683\t    // Check retry count threshold\n684\t    if retry_count < thresholds.min_retry_count {\n685\t        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n686\t            reason: format!(\n687\t                \"insufficient retries ({} < {} minimum)\",\n688\t                retry_count, thresholds.min_retry_count\n689\t            ),\n690\t        };\n691\t    }\n692\t\n693\t    // All criteria met - approve for splitting\n694\t    // The caller must add actual proposals via Split::with_proposals\n695\t    DecompositionDecision::Split {\n696\t        with_proposals: Vec::new(), // Empty - caller will populate\n697\t    }\n698\t}\n699\t\n700\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n701\t// StrandError / StrandResult\n702\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n703\t\n704\t/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n705\t#[derive(Debug)]\n706\tpub enum StrandError {\n707\t    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n708\t    ConfigError(String),\n709\t}\n710\t\n711\timpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n712\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n713\t        match self {\n714\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n715\t                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n716\t                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n717\t                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n718\t                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n719\t                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n720\t                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n721\t                }\n722\t                Ok(())\n723\t            }\n724\t            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n725\t        }\n726\t    }\n727\t}\n728\t\n729\timpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n730\t    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n731\t        match self {\n732\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n733\t            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n734\t        }\n735\t    }\n736\t}\n737\t\n738\t/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n739\t#[non_exhaustive]\n740\t#[derive(Debug)]\n741\tpub enum StrandResult {\n742\t    /// strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n747\t    NoWork,\n748\t    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n749\t    Error(StrandError),\n750\t    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n751\t    ///\n752\t    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n753\t    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). count.\n760\t    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n761\t    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n762\t    ///\n763\t    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// DecompositionMode\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Mode distinguishing timeout-driven decomposition from ordinary failure handling.\n///\n/// This enum defines the API boundary between two distinct failure-handling paths:\n/// - **Timeout mode**: Activated when a bead times out. The bead is decomposed\n///   into smaller child beads via `ChildBeadProposal`, each representing a\n///   phase of the original work. This is a recovery strategy for work that\n///   exceeded its time budget but may still be completable in smaller pieces.\n/// - **OrdinaryFailure mode**: Activated for any non-timeout failure (compilation\n///   error, test failure, agent crash, etc.). The bead is NOT decomposed.\n///   It is either retried, released, or escalated based on the failure type\n///   and consecutive failure count.\n///\n/// # When to use each mode\n///\n/// **Use `Timeout` mode when:**\n/// - An agent process exits with code 124 (GNU timeout) or times out via another wrapper\n/// - The bead has made progress but exceeded its time budget\n/// - The work can be meaningfully split into discrete phases\n/// - Child beads can complete the work with the same or reduced timeout\n///\n/// **Use `OrdinaryFailure` mode when:**\n/// - Exit codes 1-123, 125-128 (failure codes) or 127 (agent not found)\n/// - Exit codes >128 (signal crashes)\n/// - Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n/// - The failure is NOT time-related and splitting won't help\n///\n/// # API boundary\n///\n/// This enum is the sole discriminator for whether the decomposition path is\n/// activated. No other code should check timeout status or exit codes to make\n/// this decision — all decomposition logic should route through this enum.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum DecompositionMode {\n    /// Timeout-driven decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// Contains timeout-specific context for use in generating child bead\n    /// proposals (e.g., original timeout value, elapsed time, progress indicators).\n    Timeout {\n        /// The timeout duration that was exceeded (in seconds).\n        timeout_seconds: u64,\n        /// Optional hint about what phase was being worked on when timeout occurred.\n        /// This can be used to name the first child bead (e.g., \"Phase 1: Routing Rules\").\n        current_phase_hint: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// Ordinary failure mode — no decomposition.\n    ///\n    /// Used for all non-timeout failures where splitting the bead into child\n    /// beads would not help. The bead should be retried, released, or escalated\n    /// via the normal failure-handling path.\n    OrdinaryFailure,\n}\n\nimpl DecompositionMode {\n    /// Returns true if this is timeout decomposition mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the decomposition path.\n    /// All code that needs to know whether to decompose should call this method\n    /// rather than inspecting the enum directly.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: Some(\"Phase 1\".to_string()),\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(mode.is_timeout());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_timeout());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_timeout(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::Timeout { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this is ordinary failure mode.\n    ///\n    /// This is the primary query method for routing to the normal failure\n    /// handling path (retry, release, or escalate without decomposition).\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert!(mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert!(!mode.is_ordinary_failure());\n    /// ```\n    pub fn is_ordinary_failure(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure)\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the timeout duration if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the timeout value without\n    /// pattern matching. Returns `None` for `OrdinaryFailure` mode.\n    ///\n    /// # Examples\n    ///\n    /// ```\n    /// use needle::types::DecompositionMode;\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n    ///     timeout_seconds: 120,\n    ///     current_phase_hint: None,\n    /// };\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), Some(120));\n    ///\n    /// let mode = DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure;\n    /// assert_eq!(mode.timeout_seconds(), None);\n    /// ```\n    pub fn timeout_seconds(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionMode::Timeout {\n                timeout_seconds, ..\n            } => Some(*timeout_seconds),\n            DecompositionMode::OrdinaryFailure => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the current phase hint if in timeout mode, None otherwise.\n    ///\n    /// This is a convenience method for extracting the optional phase hint\n    /// without pattern matching. The decision is\n/// based on clear thresholds and bead characteristics.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DecompositionDecision {\n    /// Split the bead into the proposed child beads.\n    ///\n    /// This variant contains the proposed child beads that should be created\n    /// to complete the original work in smaller, manageable phases.\n    Split {\n        /// Proposed child beads to create.\n        with_proposals: Vec<ChildBeadProposal>,\n    },\n    /// Refuse to decompose the bead.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is returned when the bead does not meet the criteria for\n    /// decomposition. /// Returns true if this decision is to split.\n    pub fn is_split(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Split { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns true if this decision is to refuse decomposition.\n    pub fn is_refuse(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the proposals if this is a Split decision, None otherwise.\n    pub fn proposals(&self) -> Option<&Vec<ChildBeadProposal>> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { with_proposals } => Some(with_proposals),\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { .. } => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Returns the refusal reason if this is a Refuse decision, None otherwise.\n    pub fn refusal_reason(&self) -> Option<&String> {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => Some(reason),\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { .. } => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for DecompositionDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            DecompositionDecision::Split { with_proposals } => {\n                write!(f, \"split into {} child beads\", with_proposals.len())\n            }\n            DecompositionDecision::Refuse { reason } => {\n                write!(f, \"refuse: {}\", reason)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Configuration for decomposition decision thresholds.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct DecompositionThresholds {\n    /// Minimum timeout (in seconds) required to consider splitting.\n    /// Beads that timed out quickly are likely genuine errors, not size issues.\n    pub min_timeout_seconds: u64,\n    /// Minimum number of retries required to consider splitting.\n    /// Beads should be given multiple chances before decomposition.\n    pub min_retry_count: u32,\n    /// Minimum bead body length (in characters) to consider splitting.\n    /// Beads shorter than this are considered \"too small\" to split meaningfully.\n    pub min_bead_size: usize,\n    /// Labels that indicate a bead is already a child bead.\n    /// Such beads should not be split further to avoid deep nesting.\n    pub child_labels: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl Default for DecompositionThresholds {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        DecompositionThresholds {\n            min_timeout_seconds: 300, // 5 minutes\n            min_retry_count: 2,       // Must retry at least twice\n            min_bead_size: 200,       // At least 200 characters\n            child_labels: vec![\n                \"mitosis-child\".to_string(),\n                \"decomposition-child\".to_string(),\n            ],\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Evaluate whether a bead should be decomposed into child beads.\n///\n/// This function implements the decision tree for timeout-driven decomposition.\n/// It evaluates bead characteristics against configured thresholds to determine\n/// whether splitting is appropriate.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `bead` - The bead to evaluate\n/// * `timeout_seconds` - The timeout duration that was exceeded\n/// * `retry_count` - Number of consecutive retries for this bead\n/// * `thresholds` - Configuration thresholds (uses defaults if None)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `DecompositionDecision::Split` - If criteria are met (proposals must be added by caller)\n/// * `DecompositionDecision::Refuse` - If criteria are not met\n///\n/// # Decision Logic\n///\n/// **Split if ALL of these conditions are met:**\n/// - timeout_seconds >= thresholds.min_timeout_seconds\n/// - retry_count >= thresholds.min_retry_count\n/// - bead body length >= thresholds.min_bead_size\n/// - bead has no assignee (not actively being worked)\n/// - bead has no child labels (not already a decomposed child)\n///\n/// **Refuse if ANY of these conditions are met:**\n/// - Bead body is too small (< min_bead_size)\n/// - Bead has an active assignee\n/// - Bead is already a child (has child labels)\n/// - Timeout is too short (< min_timeout_seconds)\n/// - Not enough retries (< min_retry_count)\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, decompose_bead_decision};\n/// use std::path::PathBuf;\n/// use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\n///\n/// let bead = Bead {\n///     id: BeadId::from(\"needle-test\"),\n///     title: \"Test bead\".to_string(),\n///     body: Some(\"This is a substantial bead body that exceeds 200 characters...\".to_string()),\n///     priority: 2,\n///     status: BeadStatus::Open,\n///     assignee: None,\n///     labels: vec![],\n///     workspace: PathBuf::from(\"/tmp/test\"),\n///     dependencies: vec![],\n///     dependents: vec![],\n///     comments: vec![],\n///     created_at: DateTime::from_timestamp(0, 0).unwrap(),\n///     updated_at: DateTime::from_timestamp(0, 0).unwrap(),\n/// };\n///\n/// let decision = decompose_bead_decision(&bead, 600, 3, None);\n/// assert!(decision.is_split());\n/// ```\npub fn decompose_bead_decision(\n    bead: &Bead,\n    timeout_seconds: u64,\n    retry_count: u32,\n    thresholds: Option<DecompositionThresholds>,\n) -> DecompositionDecision {\n    let thresholds = thresholds.unwrap_or_default();\n\n    // Check if bead is already a child (has child labels)\n    let is_child_bead = bead\n        .labels\n        .iter()\n        .any(|label| thresholds.child_labels.contains(label));\n\n    if is_child_bead {\n        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"bead is already a child bead (has labels: {:?})\",\n                bead.labels\n                    .iter()\n                    .filter(|l| thresholds.child_labels.contains(l))\n                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Check if bead has an active assignee\n    if let Some(assignee) = &bead.assignee {\n        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n            reason: format!(\"bead has active assignee: {}\", assignee),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Check bead body size\n    let body_size = bead.body.as_ref().map(|b| b.len()).unwrap_or(0);\n    if body_size < thresholds.min_bead_size {\n        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"bead body too small ({} chars < {} minimum)\",\n                body_size, thresholds.min_bead_size\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Check timeout threshold\n    if timeout_seconds < thresholds.min_timeout_seconds {\n        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"timeout too short ({}s < {}s minimum)\",\n                timeout_seconds, thresholds.min_timeout_seconds\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Check retry count threshold\n    if retry_count < thresholds.min_retry_count {\n        return DecompositionDecision::Refuse {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"insufficient retries ({} < {} minimum)\",\n                retry_count, thresholds.min_retry_count\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // All criteria met - approve for splitting\n    // The caller must add actual proposals via Split::with_proposals\n    DecompositionDecision::Split {\n        with_proposals: Vec::new(), // Empty - caller will populate\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// The strand was skipped because its prerequisites are not met.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"ran and found nothing\")\n    /// and `Error` (which means \"ran but failed\"). `Skipped` means \"did not\n    /// run because the environment doesn't support it\" — e.g., a strand that\n    /// requires a home bead store when the worker is configured without one.\n    Skipped { reason: String },\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n    /// Candidates were found but all were excluded/assigned — short retry needed.\n    ///\n    /// This is distinct from `NoWork` (which means \"truly no candidates\").\n    /// `FoundButExcluded` means \"candidates exist but this worker can't claim\n    /// them right now\" — they're assigned to other workers or blocked by labels.\n    /// This signals the worker to use short retry backoff instead of long idle.\n    FoundButExcluded,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// Claim CLI failed with a store/CLI error (distinct from race-lost).\n    ClaimError {\n        /// Human-readable error message.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate outcome after exhausting all candidates for a selection cycle.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\n#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]\npub enum ClaimOutcome {\n    /// Successfully claimed a bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an error.\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    /// A claim error threshold was reached — bead/store is suspect.\n    ///\n    /// This variant is emitted when a bead has failed claim attempts N times\n    /// with errors (not race-lost conditions). The bead should be skipped and\n    /// marked as suspect rather than silently cycling.\n    Suspect {\n        /// The bead ID that hit the error threshold.\n        bead_id: BeadId,\n        /// The number of consecutive claim errors.\n        consecutive_errors: u32,\n        /// The most recent error message.\n        last_error: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BrDependency\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br`/`bf` JSON output, or from\n/// bead-rs's `bead` (`{\"blocker\": \"<id>\", \"kind\": \"blocks\"}` — a lean\n/// edge-only shape with no enriched title/status/priority). \"dependency_type\", alias = \"kind\", default)]\n    pub dependency_type: String,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = Option::<String>::deserialize(d)?;\n    Ok(s.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()))\n}\n\n/// A comment on a ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock contention).\n    Transient {\n        message: String,\n        bead_id: Option<BeadId>,\n    },\n    /// Bead-scoped: abandon this bead; other beads can proceed.\n    BeadScoped { message: String, bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n//      /// Flag name (e.g., `--prompt`).\n        flag: String,\n    },\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// HeartbeatFile / PeerStatus\n// a waterfall restart.\n213\t        self.beads_released > 0 || self.deps_cleaned > 0 || self.assignees_cleared > 0\n214\t    }\n215\t}\n216\t\n217\t/// The Mend strand — maintenance and This catches beads orphaned by workers\n/// that died without leaving a heartbeat file (or whose heartbeat was already\n/// cleaned up).\n///\n/// This is a store-scoped function that can be called against any BeadStore,\n/// not just the home workspace.
